Numerical experiments on nonuniform meshes demonstrate that the proposed method is robust, spectrally accurate in the azimuthal variable, and competitive in runtime with existing fast Poisson solvers. We make use of vectorization and batched BLAS/GPU-accelerated linear algebra operations to eliminate explicit loops while also formulating azimuthal and radial steps entirely in terms of dense array operations, FFTs, and NUFFTs, allowing for straightforward GPU acceleration. The implementation is released as an open-source Python package at https://github.com/CharliePyle4/NUFFTRR_Poisson, and its methodology can be extended directly to related elliptic problems such as the Helmholtz equation.

AI.tldr: This paper develops NUFFTRR, a solver for the Poisson equation on a disk that extends the classical FFTRR framework to allow nonuniform grids in both radial and azimuthal directions, using NUDFT least-squares or NUFFT-based iterative schemes, with GPU-accelerated implementation.
AI.motivation: Classical FFTRR schemes achieve O(MN log N) complexity but require a uniformly spaced azimuthal mesh. This restricts their applicability. The authors aim to support nonuniform grids while retaining the efficient structure of the FFTRR formulation.
AI.method: The azimuthal analysis-synthesis step uses either a dense NUDFT least-squares solver or two NUFFT-based iterative schemes: a Toeplitz solver with circulant-preconditioned conjugate gradients (PCG), and a PCGLS solver with Pipe-Menon density compensation. Vectorization, batched BLAS, and GPU-accelerated linear algebra eliminate explicit loops, with azimuthal and radial steps formulated via dense array operations, FFTs, and NUFFTs.
AI.result: Azimuthal complexities of O(N^3 + MN^2) for the NUDFT variant and O(K_iter MN log N) for NUFFT variants. Numerical experiments show the method is robust, spectrally accurate in azimuth, and competitive in runtime with existing fast Poisson solvers.
AI.conclusion: The proposed NUFFTRR solver handles nonuniform grids in both radial and azimuthal directions while preserving FFTRR's favorable structure, is GPU-friendly, released as an open-source Python package, and extends to related elliptic problems such as the Helmholtz equation.

title: Tomography of reactive Boltzmann kernels from product fluxes
summary: We study the reversible reaction $1+2\rightleftarrows3+4$ in a dilute gas described by a Boltzmann system. We prove that the outgoing flux of one product species determines the forward collision kernel throughout the domain on a prescribed admissible set of relative velocities and outgoing directions. The elastic collision laws are known, and the reverse kernel is fixed by a prescribed reciprocity relation. The measurements use two synchronized incoming packets with fixed relative velocity and a common velocity tending to infinity. Under bounded angularly integrated collision rates, the short transit time allows us to isolate the contribution of one forward reaction, with estimates uniform as the packets concentrate. Suitable tests of the product flux yield the spatial line integrals of the kernel and a Fourier reconstruction, without differentiating the nonlinear boundary map. We also estimate the effects of finite beam speed, packet width, detector resolution, and measurement noise on the recovered line integrals.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that the forward collision kernel of a reversible reaction 1+2⇌3+4 in a dilute Boltzmann gas can be reconstructed from measurements of one product species' outgoing flux, using synchronized incoming packets and a limiting procedure, with error estimates for experimental imperfections.
AI.motivation: The motivation is to determine the forward collision kernel of a reversible reactive Boltzmann system from observable quantities. Since the elastic collision laws are known and the reverse kernel is fixed by a reciprocity relation, the goal is to show that outgoing product flux measurements suffice to recover the forward kernel throughout the domain.
AI.method: The authors use two synchronized incoming packets with fixed relative velocity and a common velocity tending to infinity. Under bounded angularly integrated collision rates, the short transit time isolates one forward reaction. Tests of the product flux yield spatial line integrals of the kernel, enabling Fourier reconstruction without differentiating the nonlinear boundary map. They also analyze effects of finite beam speed, packet width, detector resolution, and noise.
AI.result: The outgoing flux of one product species determines the forward collision kernel on a prescribed admissible set of relative velocities and outgoing directions. Spatial line integrals of the kernel and a Fourier reconstruction are obtained, with uniform estimates as packets concentrate.
AI.conclusion: The forward collision kernel of the reversible reaction can be recovered from product flux measurements, and the recovery is robust to finite beam speed, packet width, detector resolution, and measurement noise.

title: CraftSPH: A high-accuracy and composable differentiable SPH solver implemented in PyTorch
comment: The code is publicly available at https://github.com/GenMNL/CraftSPH 43 pages, 14 figures
summary: Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) is well suited to a range of problems, particularly those involving large deformations in fluid dynamics. In recent years, in addition to the advancement of SPH formulations, the development of differentiable solvers has also progressed. However, unified frameworks that flexibly accommodate diverse numerical schemes, including advanced and implicit methods, while supporting continuous extension and updating remain limited. In this study, a high-accuracy and composable differentiable SPH solver, CraftSPH, has been developed. In CraftSPH, major computational operations are implemented as independent modules, which can be combined according to the intended purpose of constructing a solver. This design enables different computational schemes to be intuitively constructed from combinations of common components and allows newly developed high-accuracy discretization methods to be flexibly incorporated and extended. Furthermore, each module supports automatic differentiation, enabling applications to physical-parameter estimation and to optimization that combines SPH solvers with deep learning models. Accordingly, CraftSPH provides an SPH computational framework in which high-accuracy discretization, explicit and implicit computations, and automatic differentiation can be handled in a unified and extensible manner. To demonstrate the applicability of CraftSPH to a wide range of problems, forward analyses are conducted for Poiseuille flow, two- and three-dimensional dam-break problems, and a rising-bubble problem. In addition, the performance of automatic differentiation is evaluated through inverse problems involving parameter estimation for the Taylor-Green vortex and lid-driven cavity flow.

AI.tldr: CraftSPH is a high-accuracy, composable differentiable Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) solver built from independent, combinable modules, unifying diverse discretization schemes, explicit/implicit computation, and automatic differentiation.
AI.motivation: SPH suits large-deformation fluid problems, and both SPH formulations and differentiable solvers have advanced. However, unified frameworks that flexibly support diverse numerical schemes (including advanced and implicit methods) while allowing continuous extension and updating remain limited.
AI.method: Develops CraftSPH, where major computational operations are implemented as independent modules that can be combined to construct solvers. This modular design enables intuitive construction of different schemes from common components, flexible incorporation of new high-accuracy discretization methods, and automatic differentiation in each module.
AI.result: Forward analyses are conducted for Poiseuille flow, two- and three-dimensional dam-break problems, and a rising-bubble problem. Automatic differentiation performance is evaluated via inverse problems: parameter estimation for the Taylor-Green vortex and lid-driven cavity flow.
AI.conclusion: CraftSPH provides a unified, extensible SPH framework handling high-accuracy discretization, explicit and implicit computations, and automatic differentiation together, supporting applications like physical-parameter estimation and optimization combining SPH with deep learning.

title: Overdetermined problem for optimal transportation
summary: In this paper, we establish symmetry results for solutions of overdetermined problems arising in optimal transportation. These problems involve the Monge-Ampère equation with a Dirichlet boundary condition $u=0$ on $\partial Ω$ and the natural boundary condition $Du(Ω)=Ω^{*}$. We show that symmetry holds when the target is the unit ball $B$. For more general target domains, including the cases $Ω^*=Ω$ and arbitrary $Ω^{*}$, symmetry is retained under an additional volume constraint on $Ω$ and a boundary condition on $|Du|$. Finally, we introduce a curvature-type overdetermined problem for the Monge-Ampère equation and obtain ellipsoidal or spherical symmetry under an additional integral normalization condition. Our proofs rely on distinct techniques in different contexts: optimal transport and convex analysis for some cases, integral identities and isoperimetric inequalities for others, and P-function methods for the remaining cases. As a byproduct, in the $τ=2$ case, a new maximum principle for the $P$-function $φ(x)=\sum_{k,l=1}^{n}{\frac{\partial{S_τ(D^2{u})}}{\partial{u_{kl}}}u_{k}u_{l}}-2\binom{n-1}{τ-1}\int_{0}^{u}{f^{\fracτ{n}}(t)\,dt}$ is established for arbitrary positive and nondecreasing $f$, which is of independent interest.

AI.tldr: We establish symmetry results for solutions of overdetermined problems arising in optimal transportation, involving the Monge-Ampère equation with Dirichlet boundary condition u=0 on ∂Ω and natural boundary condition Du(Ω)=Ω*. Symmetry holds when the target is the unit ball; for more general targets, symmetry is retained under additional volume and boundary conditions. We also introduce a curvature-type overdetermined problem and obtain (ellipsoidal or spherical) symmetry.
AI.motivation: Overdetermined problems like Serrin's problem have classical symmetry results, but analogous problems for the Monge-Ampère equation arising in optimal transportation are less understood. The paper aims to extend symmetry results to this framework.
AI.method: The proofs use different techniques: optimal transport and convex analysis; integral identities and isoperimetric inequalities; and P-function methods. As a byproduct, a new maximum principle for a P-function is established in the τ=2 case.
AI.result: Symmetry is shown when Ω* is the unit ball. For general targets (including Ω*=Ω and arbitrary Ω*), symmetry holds under an additional volume constraint on Ω and a boundary condition on |Du|. A curvature-type overdetermined problem yields ellipsoidal or spherical symmetry under an integral normalization. A new maximum principle for the P-function holds for arbitrary positive nondecreasing f (τ=2).
AI.conclusion: The paper extends overdetermined symmetry results to optimal-transport Monge-Ampère problems, with the P-function maximum principle being of independent interest.

title: Catheter-modulated transient solute dispersion in micropolar annular flow with a retentive and absorptive arterial wall
summary: We study transient solute dispersion in pressure-driven micropolar flow through a concentric annulus representing a catheterized artery. The catheter is impermeable to solute, whereas the arterial wall combines irreversible removal with reversible surface retention. The exact steady micropolar velocity field is coupled to the Gill-Sankarasubramanian generalized-dispersion framework; the resulting bulk-surface hierarchy is advanced with Rannacher-damped Crank-Nicolson time stepping to determine $K_0(t)$, $K_1(t)$ and $K_2(t)$. The exchange coefficient is independent of the micropolar parameters and satisfies $-K_0(0^+)=2(β+θDa)/(1-λ^2)$, whereas $K_2-Pe^{-2}\simσ_v^2t$ initially, so the leading short-time dispersion is hydrodynamic and independent of wall kinetics. In the weak-reaction regime, micropolarity modifies convection approximately linearly and shear dispersion quadratically through the velocity-amplitude factor. A narrow-gap analysis with $\varepsilon=1-λ$ gives $\bar v\sim(2-N_c)\varepsilon^2/6$ and $K_2-Pe^{-2}\sim(2-N_c)^2\varepsilon^6/7560$ for a fixed pressure gradient, revealing a sixth-power suppression of shear dispersion as the catheter approaches the arterial wall. Increasing $λ$ from $0.01$ to $0.30$ reduces effective convection by about a factor of $2.45$, while chemically passive shear-induced dispersion falls by a factor of $24$. The coupled formulation also yields the exact partition $Φ_m+Φ_s+Φ_a=1$, separating mobile, reversibly retained and irreversibly absorbed solute. The reconstructed field quantifies reaction-modulated transverse non-uniformity, while the results distinguish hydrodynamic effects of confinement and microrotation from kinetic wall effects.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes transient solute dispersion in pressure-driven micropolar flow through a concentric annulus modeling a catheterized artery, coupling the exact micropolar velocity field with the Gill-Sankarasubramanian dispersion framework and irreversible/reversible wall kinetics.
AI.motivation: To understand how micropolar (microstructure-induced) fluid effects, annular confinement by a catheter, and combined irreversible removal plus reversible surface retention of solute together govern transient dispersion in a catheterized artery.
AI.method: The exact steady micropolar velocity field for a concentric annulus is coupled to the Gill-Sankarasubramanian generalized-dispersion framework. The resulting bulk-surface hierarchy is advanced numerically with Rannacher-damped Crank-Nicolson time stepping to obtain K0(t), K1(t), K2(t), supported by a narrow-gap asymptotic analysis with small epsilon = 1 - lambda.
AI.result: The exchange coefficient is independent of micropolar parameters, satisfying -K0(0+) = 2(beta + theta Da)/(1 - lambda^2), and K2 - Pe^-2 ~ sigma_v^2 t initially, so short-time leading dispersion is hydrodynamic and wall-kinetics-independent. Micropolarity modifies convection roughly linearly and shear dispersion quadratically in the weak-reaction regime. Narrow-gap analysis gives vbar ~ (2 - Nc) epsilon^2/6 and K2 - Pe^-2 ~ (2 - Nc)^2 epsilon^6/7560, showing sixth-power suppression of shear dispersion. Raising lambda from 0.01 to 0.30 cuts effective convection ~2.45x and passive shear dispersion ~24x, and yields the exact partition Phi_m + Phi_s + Phi_a = 1.
AI.conclusion: The coupled formulation separates mobile, reversibly retained, and irreversibly absorbed solute, quantifies reaction-modulated transverse non-uniformity, and distinguishes hydrodynamic effects of confinement and microrotation from kinetic wall effects.

title: Improved existence time for a Boussinesq system
summary: We consider a strongly dispersive Boussinesq-type system arising as a model for the propagation of weakly nonlinear water waves. The system is characterized by a nonlinearity parameter $0<ε\le 1$ and a shallow water parameter $0<μ\le 1$. In the Boussinesq regime $μ\sim ε$, Saut, Wang and Xu \cite{SWX2017} used a hyperbolic approach to prove the well-posedness of the system on a time scale of order $1/ε$, in both one and two dimensions, under a non-cavitation condition. In this paper, we establish well-posedness on a time scale of order $ ( μ^{ 1/4} ε^{-1} h_0 )^{4/3}$ in one dimension and of order $(μ^{ 1/4}ε^{-1} h_0)^{2-}$ in two dimensions, assuming a non-cavitation condition with a parameter $h_0>0$. Our results show quantitatively how the lifespan depends on the balance between nonlinearity and dispersion in the regimes $ε\lesssim μ$ and $μ\llε$. They also make explicit how the existence time deteriorates as $h_0\to0$, that is, as the wave approaches cavitation. Our proofs combine dispersive and Strichartz estimates with energy estimates.

AI.tldr: This paper proves well-posedness for a strongly dispersive Boussinesq-type water wave system on longer time scales than previously known, showing explicitly how the lifespan depends on nonlinearity, dispersion, and proximity to cavitation.
AI.motivation: The Boussinesq system models weakly nonlinear water waves with parameters ε (nonlinearity) and μ (shallowness). Prior work by Saut, Wang, and Xu proved well-posedness on time scale 1/ε in the Boussinesq regime μ~ε. This paper aims to extend the existence time and quantify how the lifespan depends on the balance between nonlinearity and dispersion, as well as how it deteriorates near cavitation.
AI.method: Combines dispersive estimates and Strichartz estimates with energy estimates, assuming a non-cavitation condition parameterized by h_0>0.
AI.result: Establishes well-posedness on a time scale of order (μ^{1/4} ε^{-1} h_0)^{4/3} in one dimension and (μ^{1/4} ε^{-1} h_0)^{2-} in two dimensions, quantitatively showing lifespan dependence on the balance between nonlinearity and dispersion in regimes ε≲μ and μ≪ε, and on h_0→0 as cavitation approaches.
AI.conclusion: The results improve and refine earlier well-posedness time scales, making explicit the trade-off between nonlinearity, dispersion, and cavitation proximity for the Boussinesq-type system.

title: High-accuracy simulation of Picard HMC, part I: Gaussian cloud correction
summary: We study the problem of sampling from a continuous density $π\propto \exp(-V)$ on $\mathbb R^d$, where $V\in C^2(\mathbb R^d)$ has a $β$-Lipschitz gradient and $π$ satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality with constant $α^{-1}$, and write $κ= β/α$. We introduce the Gaussian cloud sampler, which achieves total variation accuracy $\varepsilon$ using $\widetilde O(κd^{1/5}\,\text{polylog}(1/\varepsilon))$ gradient queries in expectation. The algorithm uses first-order rejection sampling (FORS) to correct the law of smoothed Picard HMC trajectories. To do so, we represent the iterates of the ideal Picard iteration via Gaussian clouds, whose centers are never evaluated, and we develop a suite of likelihood correction gadgets which only use samples from this indirect cloud representation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the "Gaussian cloud sampler" for sampling from a continuous density π ∝ exp(-V) on R^d, achieving total variation accuracy ε using Õ(κd^{1/5} polylog(1/ε)) gradient queries in expectation.
AI.motivation: Sampling from continuous densities in high dimensions is a fundamental problem, and existing methods often suffer from poor dimension dependence. The goal is to achieve better complexity in terms of dimension d and condition number κ = β/α.
AI.method: The algorithm uses first-order rejection sampling (FORS) to correct the law of smoothed Picard HMC trajectories. It represents iterates of the ideal Picard iteration via Gaussian clouds whose centers are never evaluated, and develops likelihood correction gadgets using only samples from this indirect cloud representation.
AI.result: The Gaussian cloud sampler achieves TV accuracy ε using Õ(κd^{1/5} polylog(1/ε)) gradient queries in expectation. Notably, the dimension dependence d^{1/5} is a substantial improvement over typical dependencies.
AI.conclusion: The Gaussian cloud sampler provides an efficient sampling algorithm with improved dimension dependence by leveraging FORS and indirect Gaussian cloud representations to correct Picard HMC trajectories.

title: Low Mach number limit of a two-phase flow model in $\mathbb{R}^3$
summary: We study the simultaneous low Mach number limit of a compressible Navier--Stokes--Euler two-phase system in $\mathbb R^3$, in which the pressure terms in both phases are scaled by $\varepsilon^{-2}$. For sufficiently small $H^3$-perturbations around the constant equilibrium, we establish the global well-posedness of the scaled compressible system and derive global energy-dissipation estimates that are uniform with respect to the Mach number $\varepsilon$. A key feature of the analysis is the degenerate dissipation structure: viscosity acts only on the Navier--Stokes phase, while the drag coupling transfers dissipation to the inviscid Euler phase through the relaxation mode. We then prove the global well-posedness and large-time decay of the limiting incompressible two-phase system, and show that the relative velocity $u-ω$ decays faster than the full velocity pair. Finally, for the well-prepared initial data, we introduce pressure-corrected acoustic variables to remove the singular pressure mismatch and establish a global-in-time $H^2$-error. As a result, the scaled compressible solutions converge uniformly in time to the corresponding solution of the limiting incompressible system.

AI.tldr: Global low Mach number limit of a compressible Navier-Stokes-Euler two-phase system in R^3, with uniform energy estimates, decay, and convergence to the incompressible limit.
AI.motivation: To understand the simultaneous low Mach number limit of a compressible two-phase system where only one phase is viscous, and how dissipation transfers to the inviscid phase via drag coupling.
AI.method: Scaling pressure terms by epsilon^-2; using H^3-perturbations around equilibrium; degenerate dissipation analysis with drag relaxation; pressure-corrected acoustic variables for well-prepared data.
AI.result: Global well-posedness and epsilon-uniform energy-dissipation estimates; global well-posedness and large-time decay of the limiting incompressible system; faster decay of relative velocity; global-in-time H^2-error and uniform convergence for well-prepared data.
AI.conclusion: The scaled compressible solutions converge uniformly in time to the limiting incompressible two-phase system, with a global-in-time H^2 error for well-prepared data.

title: ABrA-GD: Adaptive Bregman Accelerated Gradient Descent for Relatively Smooth and (Strongly-)Convex Optimization
summary: We propose ABrA-GD (Adaptive Bregman Accelerated Gradient Descent), an adaptive algorithm for relatively smooth convex optimization. The algorithm is derived from a computable primal--dual certificate that guarantees progress by comparing the objective value with a lower bound on the minimum of a regularized objective. This certificate enables adaptation to both smoothness and geometry, using only the relative strong convexity constant as a problem-dependent input. We introduce the dual Bregman Length Distortion Factor (BLDF), which measures how dual Bregman lengths change under an anchor shift or rescaling. Under bounded local dual BLDF, ABrA-GD achieves an accelerated $O(1/k^2)$ rate for convex objectives and an accelerated linear rate for relatively strongly convex objectives.

AI.tldr: ABrA-GD is an adaptive Bregman accelerated gradient method for relatively smooth convex optimization, using a primal-dual certificate to adapt to smoothness and geometry and achieving O(1/k^2) or linear rates.
AI.motivation: Optimization algorithms need to adapt to both smoothness and geometry of the problem while maintaining acceleration, which is challenging in the relatively smooth setting.
AI.method: Derives the algorithm from a computable primal-dual certificate comparing the objective value with a lower bound on a regularized objective's minimum. Introduces the dual Bregman Length Distortion Factor (BLDF) to measure how dual Bregman lengths change under anchor shifts/rescaling, requiring only the relative strong convexity constant.
AI.result: Under bounded local dual BLDF, achieves accelerated O(1/k^2) rate for convex objectives and accelerated linear rate for relatively strongly convex objectives.
AI.conclusion: ABrA-GD provides a certificate-based framework enabling adaptive, accelerated convergence in relatively smooth convex optimization.

title: Global existence for Consensus-Based Kinetic Models for Image Segmentation
summary: In this article, we analyze a recently introduced kinetic model based on Hegselmann-Krause-type interaction dynamics describing consensus-based image segmentation in the mean-field regime, where particle density depends on spatial coordinates and the normalized gray level (feature) value. The model is formulated as an evolutive nonlocal partial differential equation featuring a non-local spatial drift term involving a bounded confidence interaction kernel, depending on spatial and feature proximity, and a spatial diffusion term degenerating in the feature variable representing aleatoric uncertainties. Establishing well-posedness on a bounded domain, essential for practical image processing, presents significant analytical challenges: the lack of uniform control of space derivatives due to kernels with jump discontinuities and degenerate spatial diffusion, complex non-standard boundary terms under homogeneous Neumann conditions, and a lack of compactness arising from the absence of derivatives with respect to the feature variable. To address these difficulties, we introduce a three-level regularization scheme. Specifically, we smooth the interaction kernel, apply structural boundary regularization to the non-local interaction term to simplify boundary conditions, and incorporate artificial diffusion in spatial and feature variables to resolve degeneracy. We prove the well-posedness and regularity of the regularized system via a finite difference scheme and study the asymptotic limit as regularization parameters vanish, proving the existence of weak/distributional solutions of the original model. This approach advances the mathematical theory of kinetic models for image segmentation by extending the framework of distributional solutions to bounded domains and non-smooth interaction kernels with jump discontinuities.

AI.tldr: The paper proves well-posedness of a kinetic Hegselmann-Krause-type model for consensus-based image segmentation, formulated as a nonlocal degenerate PDE on a bounded domain, via a three-level regularization scheme.
AI.motivation: The model describes mean-field image segmentation where particle density depends on space and normalized gray level. Proving well-posedness on a bounded domain (needed for image processing) is hard due to jump-discontinuous kernels, degenerate diffusion, non-standard boundary terms, and lack of compactness in the feature variable.
AI.method: A three-level regularization scheme: (1) smoothing the interaction kernel, (2) structural boundary regularization of the nonlocal interaction term to simplify Neumann boundary conditions, and (3) artificial diffusion in spatial and feature variables to resolve degeneracy. Well-posedness/regularity of the regularized system is proven via a finite difference scheme, then the asymptotic limit as regularization parameters vanish is studied.
AI.result: Well-posedness and regularity of the regularized system are established, and existence of weak/distributional solutions of the original model is proven in the vanishing-regularization limit.
AI.conclusion: The approach advances the mathematical theory of kinetic image segmentation models by extending the distributional-solution framework to bounded domains and non-smooth interaction kernels with jump discontinuities.

title: Halpern-Accelerated Majorized ADMM with Optimal Non-Ergodic Convergence under Degenerate Preconditioning
summary: We develop a Halpern-accelerated majorized alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with possibly indefinite proximal terms for linearly constrained convex composite optimization. Majorization simplifies the subproblems but introduces a forward perturbation to the standard degenerate proximal point representation. We reformulate majorized ADMM as a perturbed degenerate proximal point method and characterize the fixed points of the induced mapping as Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) solutions. Under range compatibility and metric cocoercivity conditions, the mapping is nonexpansive in the seminorm induced by a possibly singular preconditioner. In finite dimensions, a verifiable block-matrix condition permits indefinite proximal regularization while retaining the required metric properties. A relaxed Halpern iteration then yields an $\mathcal O(1/k)$ fixed-point residual bound, sharp in the general nonexpansive setting, and an $\mathcal O(1/k)$ nonergodic KKT residual bound at the intermediate iterates. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted residual decay and the benefits of majorization and indefinite proximal terms.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a Halpern-accelerated majorized ADMM with possibly indefinite proximal terms for linearly constrained convex composite optimization, proving O(1/k) convergence rates for both fixed-point and nonergodic KKT residuals.
AI.motivation: Majorization simplifies ADMM subproblems but introduces a forward perturbation to the standard degenerate proximal point representation, requiring new analysis to understand the induced mapping and its convergence properties.
AI.method: The authors reformulate majorized ADMM as a perturbed degenerate proximal point method, characterize fixed points of the induced mapping as KKT solutions, and establish nonexpansiveness under range compatibility and metric cocoercivity conditions. A verifiable block-matrix condition allows indefinite proximal regularization while preserving metric properties, and a relaxed Halpern iteration is applied.
AI.result: The relaxed Halpern iteration yields an O(1/k) fixed-point residual bound (sharp in the general nonexpansive setting) and an O(1/k) nonergodic KKT residual bound at intermediate iterates. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted residual decay and the benefits of majorization and indefinite proximal terms.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully combines majorization, indefinite proximal terms, and Halpern acceleration within ADMM, achieving provable O(1/k) convergence rates verified by numerical experiments.

title: Inverting the geodesic ray transform with finite measurements: stability and reconstruction
summary: We study the inversion of the geodesic ray transform from finitely many local averages of its data. Under suitable geometric assumptions, we prove Lipschitz stability on any fixed finite-dimensional reconstruction space when the measurement partition is sufficiently fine. We develop convergent reconstruction algorithms based on Steepest Gradient Descent and Conjugate Gradients and implement them using piecewise constant finite element spaces. Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D illustrate the influence of geometry and measurement discretization on reconstruction quality.

AI.tldr: The paper proves Lipschitz stability and develops convergent reconstruction algorithms for inverting the geodesic ray transform using finitely many local averages of its data.
AI.motivation: Inverting the geodesic ray transform typically requires complete data, but practical settings only provide finitely many local averages. There is a need to understand stability and to have reliable reconstruction algorithms under such limited measurement conditions.
AI.method: Under suitable geometric assumptions, the authors prove Lipschitz stability on any fixed finite-dimensional reconstruction space when the measurement partition is sufficiently fine. They develop convergent reconstruction algorithms based on Steepest Gradient Descent and Conjugate Gradients, implemented with piecewise constant finite element spaces.
AI.result: Lipschitz stability is established for sufficiently fine measurement partitions. Numerical experiments in 2D and 3D illustrate how geometry and measurement discretization influence reconstruction quality.
AI.conclusion: The inversion from finitely many local averages is stable and tractable, and the proposed gradient-based algorithms with finite element discretization give effective reconstructions, with quality governed by geometric and discretization factors.

title: Minimax rates for learning spectral Barron functions by deep ReLU neural networks
summary: We study how well deep neural networks approximate and learn spectral Barron functions. Recent studies have shown that these function classes can be efficiently approximated by shallow neural networks without suffering from the curse of dimensionality. We complement these results by providing new approximation bounds for deep networks with ReLU activation and establishing the minimax rates for learning these function classes. Specifically, we show that $d$-dimensional spectral Barron functions with smoothness index $s>0$ can be approximated by deep ReLU neural networks with approximation rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}} (S^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{s}{d}})$, where $S$ denotes the number of nonzero parameters in the network. Using this approximation result, we further show that deep ReLU neural networks can learn spectral Barron functions in a fast rate $n^{-\frac{d+2s}{2d+2s}}$ with $n$ training samples. Finally, we prove that this convergence rate is minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors.

AI.tldr: The paper studies approximation and learning of spectral Barron functions by deep ReLU networks, providing new approximation bounds and establishing minimax optimal learning rates.
AI.motivation: Recent work shows shallow networks can efficiently approximate spectral Barron functions without the curse of dimensionality. The authors complement this by analyzing deep ReLU networks, addressing the gap in approximation bounds and learning rates for these function classes.
AI.method: They derive new approximation bounds for deep ReLU networks with $S$ nonzero parameters, showing $d$-dimensional spectral Barron functions with smoothness index $s>0$ are approximated at rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(S^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{s}{d}})$. They then use this to analyze learning with $n$ training samples.
AI.result: Deep ReLU networks approximate spectral Barron functions at rate $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(S^{-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{s}{d}})$ and learn them at rate $n^{-\frac{d+2s}{2d+2s}}$. This rate is proven minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors.
AI.conclusion: Deep ReLU networks efficiently approximate and learn spectral Barron functions, achieving minimax optimal convergence rates up to logarithmic factors.

title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
summary: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.

AI.tldr: This paper extends prior Kerr stability results from the slowly rotating regime (|a|≪m) to the full subextremal range (|a|<m), completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture.
AI.motivation: Previous work by Klainerman and collaborators (and Shen) proved Kerr stability only for slowly rotating black holes (|a|≪m). Removing this restriction to cover the full subextremal range |a|<m is needed to complete the Kerr stability conjecture.
AI.method: Extends the earlier sequence of works by relying on two companion papers (with Siyuan Ma) proving energy-Morawetz estimates for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with |a|<m; the |a|≪m restriction entered only through wave-equation and Bianchi-system estimates from GKS22.
AI.result: Establishes stability of Kerr for the full subextremal range |a|<m, completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. Some results are also proved in companion paper [Sze].
AI.conclusion: The Kerr stability conjecture is now fully resolved across the entire subextremal range, extending from slow rotation to |a|<m.

title: LampAttention: Look-Ahead Mixed-Precision FlashAttention for Dedicated Accelerators
summary: While most attention logits can be computed in low precision without degrading numerical stability, current attention kernels fail to exploit this phenomenon. We introduce a novel hardware-algorithm co-design in the form of mixed-precision FlashAttention. Our method accumulates key-query products and evaluates their exponentials in 8-bit formats, then adaptively identifies sensitive sub-blocks and recomputes them in 16-bit formats. We propose the specifications for a dedicated accelerator capable of executing this pipeline efficiently. Simulated experiments with Qwen3 and Gemma 3 show that rerouting a selective minority of sub-blocks to high precision is sufficient to recover the baseline model performance.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes mixed-precision FlashAttention, a hardware-algorithm co-design that computes most attention in 8-bit and selectively recomputes sensitive sub-blocks in 16-bit, with a dedicated accelerator spec, recovering baseline performance on Qwen3 and Gemma 3.
AI.motivation: Most attention logits can be computed in low precision without hurting numerical stability, but existing attention kernels do not exploit this, wasting efficiency.
AI.method: A mixed-precision FlashAttention pipeline: accumulate key-query products and evaluate exponentials in 8-bit, then adaptively detect sensitive sub-blocks and recompute them in 16-bit. Specifications for a dedicated hardware accelerator to run this pipeline are proposed.
AI.result: Simulated experiments with Qwen3 and Gemma 3 show that rerouting a selective minority of sub-blocks to high precision suffices to recover baseline model performance.
AI.conclusion: Selective mixed-precision recomputation enables efficient attention acceleration while preserving accuracy, motivating dedicated accelerator hardware.

title: Dispersion for the wave equation with Neumann boundary condition inside general strictly convex domains
summary: We consider the wave equation on a manifold of dimension d>1 with smooth strictly convex boundary, with Neumann boundary condition. We construct a sharp local in time parametrix for the Neumann wave equation near glancing, extending the classical Melrose-Taylor construction for the Dirichlet problem to the Neumann boundary condition. Our construction is based on the microlocal framework and the parametrix developed in [10] for the Dirichlet problem, together with the Melrose-Taylor argument for solving the transport equations under more general, affine-type boundary conditions. Once the Neumann parametrix is constructed, the dispersive and Strichartz estimates follow the analysis developed in [10] for the Dirichlet problem. We therefore only recall the main ingredients of that argument. In particular, the fixed time decay rate for the Green function exhibits the same loss of 1/4 with respect to the boundaryless case, associated with swallowtail type singularities in the wave front set, and this decay is optimal. Moreover, the corresponding Strichartz estimates are obtained by balancing lossy long time estimates at a given incidence with short time ones with no loss: for d=3, this heuristically means that, on average, the decay loss is only 1/6 .

AI.tldr: Sharp local-in-time parametrix for the Neumann wave equation near glancing on a strictly convex domain, extending Melrose-Taylor from Dirichlet to Neumann, yielding optimal dispersive/Strichartz estimates.
AI.motivation: The classical Melrose-Taylor parametrix handles the Dirichlet wave equation near glancing, but the Neumann case was not covered. Extending it is needed to obtain sharp dispersive and Strichartz estimates for the Neumann boundary condition.
AI.method: Build a microlocal sharp local-in-time parametrix near glancing using the framework of [10] for Dirichlet, combined with a Melrose-Taylor argument to solve transport equations under more general affine-type boundary conditions. Then adapt the Dirichlet dispersive/Strichartz analysis.
AI.result: Fixed-time Green function decay loses 1/4 versus the boundaryless case, tied to swallowtail-type wave front singularities; the decay is optimal. Strichartz estimates follow from balancing lossy long-time and lossless short-time estimates—for d=3, average loss is only 1/6.
AI.conclusion: The Neumann glancing parametrix can be constructed analogously to Dirichlet, and it delivers optimal dispersive and Strichartz estimates with quantified (often smaller on average) decay losses.

title: Computing Extinction Barriers in a Quorum-Sensing Reaction Network
comment: 26 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to the MMSC 2026 proceedings (EPiC Series in Computing). Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23062342
summary: We introduce a simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population that couples the cell density $x$ to the signal density $w$. In the four-channel cell-signal network studied here, scaling signal production and removal by the same factor $r$ leaves all deterministic equilibria, and their stability types, unchanged. Nevertheless, we show that $r$ shifts the quasipotential barrier $ΔV(r)$ for rare transitions towards extinction, and thus, under metastable exit assumptions, the mean time to reach a fixed neighbourhood of the extinction state on the exponential scale $e^{NΔV(r)}$. We compute the barrier by minimization of the path action with the signal retained as a fluctuating coordinate, and we compare it with exact stochastic simulation of population-threshold crossing times regressed in $N$. Over a range of $r$, the minimum-action barriers satisfy $ΔV(r)=ΔV_\infty+O(1/r)$, where $ΔV_\infty$ is obtained by eliminating the signal first. At $r=1$, the barrier is 55% larger than $ΔV_\infty$. The saddle barrier $ΔV(r)$ is also the least action needed to enter the basin of extinction, but the density threshold can be crossed more cheaply: at $r=0.5$ the cheapest crossing costs 7.7% less action, keeps the signal high, and is usually followed by recovery. Simulated arrival times in this neighbourhood, which include failed attempts, grow with slopes within two fitted standard errors of the saddle barrier at every tested rate, and within $0.004$ of it if the logarithmic prefactor term is omitted. Under either regression model they exclude $ΔV_\infty$ at $r\le2$ by at least $4.4$ fitted standard errors, without using the action solver.

AI.tldr: A reaction-network model links cell density x to signal density w; scaling both signal production and removal by r leaves deterministic equilibria and their stability unchanged, yet changes the quasipotential barrier for extinction by ΔV(r)=ΔV∞+O(1/r), altering mean extinction times on the e^{NΔV(r)} scale.
AI.motivation: Scaling signal production and removal by the same factor r preserves all deterministic equilibria and their stability types, so one might expect no effect on extinction. The paper asks whether such a scaling nonetheless affects rare-transition (extinction) dynamics, and specifically whether the signal, retained as a fluctuating coordinate, matters for the quasipotential barrier.
AI.method: A simple reaction-network model of a quorum-sensing population coupling cell density x to signal density w in a four-channel cell-signal network. The quasipotential barrier is computed by minimization of the path action with the signal treated as a fluctuating coordinate (rather than eliminated), and results are compared with exact stochastic simulation of population-threshold crossing times regressed in N.
AI.result: Deterministic equilibria and stability types are unchanged by r, but the barrier ΔV(r) shifts. Over a range of r, minimum-action barriers satisfy ΔV(r)=ΔV∞+O(1/r), with ΔV∞ from eliminating the signal first; at r=1 the barrier is 55% larger than ΔV∞. At r=0.5 the cheapest density-threshold crossing costs 7.7% less action, keeps signal high, and usually recovers. Simulated arrival times grow with slopes within two fitted standard errors of the saddle barrier at every tested rate (within 0.004 if the logarithmic prefactor is omitted), and exclude ΔV∞ at r≤2 by at least 4.4 standard errors without using the action solver.
AI.conclusion: Scaling signal production and removal by r leaves deterministic equilibria and stability untouched, but materially changes the rare-transition barrier and hence extinction times. The signal cannot generally be eliminated: retaining it as a fluctuating coordinate yields barriers that agree with simulation and differ significantly from the reduced ΔV∞, underscoring the role of fluctuations in the eliminated coordinate for metastable extinction.

title: Topological invariants for anisotropic quasilinear elliptic systems: A Poincaré-Hopf formula
comment: To appear on Differential and Integral Equations
summary:
We consider the functional $I_{δ,Ψ_1,Ψ_2}:X \to \mathbb{R}$ defined for any $z=(u,v) \in X$ as \begin{align*}
  I_{δ,Ψ_1,Ψ_2}(z)
  & = \int_Ω Ψ_1(\nabla u) \, dx + \int_Ω Ψ_2(\nabla v ) \, dx
  & - \int_Ω
  H(δ,x,u(x),v(x)) \,dx, \end{align*} where $Ω$ is a smooth bounded domain of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $Ψ_1, Ψ_2: \mathbb{R}^N \to \mathbb{R}$ are convex functions satisfying suitable conditions for $1 < p, q < N$, and the nonlinearity $H$ is allowed to exhibit both subcritical and critical growth and may depend on a parameter $δ\in I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$. Here, the functional space setting is given by the product space $X :=W_0^{1,p}(Ω)\times W_0^{1,q}(Ω)$ equipped with the norm $\|z\|= \|u\|_{1,p} + \|v\|_{1,q}$ for any $z=(u,v)\in X$, where $\| \cdot \|_{1,s}$ is the usual norm in $W^{1,s}_0(Ω)$. In this paper we prove that $I_{δ,Ψ_1,Ψ_2}'$ is of class $(S)_+$ and we infer that each isolated critical point of $I_{δ,Ψ_1,Ψ_2}$ has critical
  groups of finite type and a Poincaré-Hopf formula holds.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that the gradient of a coupled variational functional with convex gradient terms and critical/subcritical nonlinearity is of class (S)_+, implying isolated critical points have finite-type critical groups and satisfy a Poincaré-Hopf formula.
AI.motivation: Variational functionals coupling two gradient terms with critical nonlinearities arise in systems like p-Laplacian/q-Laplacian problems. Standard critical point theory requires compactness-type conditions such as (S)_+ to extract convergence and apply Morse-theoretic tools.
AI.method: Works in X = W_0^{1,p}(Ω) × W_0^{1,q}(Ω) with convex Ψ_1, Ψ_2 and 1<p,q<N. Proves the Fréchet derivative I'_{δ,Ψ1,Ψ2} is of class (S)_+, then applies critical group theory (Morse theory) to the resulting functional.
AI.result: I'_{δ,Ψ1,Ψ2} is of class (S)_+. Each isolated critical point of the functional has critical groups of finite type, and a Poincaré-Hopf formula holds.
AI.conclusion: The (S)_+ property provides the compactness framework needed to carry over critical group/Morse-theoretic results to this class of coupled convex-gradient functionals, enabling homological analysis of their critical points.

title: Hadamard Local Well-Posedness for Compressible Liquids with a Free Surface
summary: We prove local well-posedness in the Hadamard sense for the three-dimensional compressible Euler equations governing a liquid with a free surface and no surface tension. Under the Taylor sign condition and the boundary compatibility conditions, we establish existence, uniqueness, and strong continuous dependence in a hybrid Sobolev class for every $s>3$. The velocity and interface have $H^s$ regularity, while the enthalpy and velocity divergence belong to $H^{s+1/2}$ and $H^{s-1/2}$, respectively. This separation reflects the coupling of a nondegenerate acoustic equation with the free-surface and vorticity dynamics. The proof uses regularization operators that smooth the moving domain and extend the nonlinear compatibility hierarchy, together with $L^2$ and partial $H^2$ distance estimates for solutions on different domains. Regular solutions are constructed by a regularized forward Euler scheme. High-order energy estimates and frequency envelopes then yield strong convergence of smooth approximations and continuity of the data-to-solution map. Integer Sobolev indices are treated using a Lions--Magenes endpoint compatibility condition.

AI.tldr: The paper proves local Hadamard well-posedness for the 3D compressible Euler equations with a free surface and no surface tension, in a hybrid Sobolev class for every s>3.
AI.motivation: To establish existence, uniqueness, and strong continuous dependence for the free-surface compressible Euler equations (a liquid with a free boundary and no surface tension), addressing the coupling of acoustic, free-surface, and vorticity dynamics.
AI.method: Under the Taylor sign condition and boundary compatibility conditions, the authors use regularization operators that smooth the moving domain and extend the nonlinear compatibility hierarchy, combined with L2 and partial H2 distance estimates on differing domains. Regular solutions are built via a regularized forward Euler scheme; high-order energy estimates and frequency envelopes give strong convergence and continuity. Integer Sobolev indices are handled via a Lions–Magenes endpoint compatibility condition.
AI.result: Local Hadamard well-posedness is proved for every s>3: the velocity and interface have Hs regularity, while enthalpy is in Hs+1/2 and velocity divergence in Hs-1/2, reflecting the coupling of a nondegenerate acoustic equation with free-surface and vorticity dynamics.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid regularity structure and the techniques (domain-smoothing regularization, distance estimates, energy estimates, frequency envelopes) yield well-posedness and continuity of the data-to-solution map for the free-surface compressible Euler equations.

title: adapol: Adaptive pole-fitting for quantum many-body physics
summary: We describe adapol, a Python package for fitting Matsubara Green's functions, self-energies, and hybridization functions by a compact sum of simple poles with real pole locations and matrix-valued residues. This pole-fitting step arises in many contexts, including hybridization fitting for quantum impurity solvers based on exact diagonalization, perturbation theory, and tensor networks, the compression of existing pole expansions such as the discrete Lehmann representation, diagrammatic methods based on discrete pole representations, and the analytic continuation of Matsubara Green's functions. adapol uses a modified version of the AAA rational approximation algorithm to estimate pole locations, and non-convex optimization to refine them. This procedure yields accurate and compact fits in a black-box and noise-robust manner. adapol provides a simple, self-contained interface with extensive documentation and examples, as well as an interface to the TRIQS package.

AI.tldr: adapol is a Python package that fits Matsubara Green's functions, self-energies, and hybridization functions using a compact sum of simple poles with real locations and matrix-valued residues, employing a modified AAA rational approximation and non-convex refinement.
AI.motivation: Pole-fitting arises in many contexts such as hybridization fitting for quantum impurity solvers, compression of existing pole expansions, diagrammatic methods, and analytic continuation. A robust, black-box tool is needed for accurate and compact fits.
AI.method: The package uses a modified version of the AAA rational approximation algorithm to estimate pole locations, followed by non-convex optimization to refine them, yielding accurate and compact fits in a black-box and noise-robust manner.
AI.result: adapol provides accurate and compact fits of Matsubara Green's functions, self-energies, and hybridization functions, with a simple self-contained interface, extensive documentation and examples, and an interface to TRIQS.
AI.conclusion: adapol is a practical, well-documented Python tool for pole-fitting in quantum many-body contexts, with robust fitting and interoperability with TRIQS.

title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
summary: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.

AI.tldr: This companion paper supplies proofs for two previously unproven results in \cite{Sze}: the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr, and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky, completing technical gaps in the full subextremal Kerr stability proof.
AI.motivation: The Kerr stability conjecture was recently proved across the full subextremal range |a| < m, with the final proof \cite{Sze} relying on companion works proving energy-Morawetz estimates for scalar wave and Teukolsky equations. However, two key results in \cite{Sze} were stated without proofs, leaving the argument incomplete.
AI.method: The paper provides detailed proofs of two results from \cite{Sze}: (1) the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr, and (2) energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}.
AI.result: Full proofs are supplied for the two previously unproven results, thereby completing the technical foundation of the Kerr stability proof in the full subextremal range.
AI.conclusion: This companion paper closes the remaining gaps in \cite{Sze}, ensuring the completeness of the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture for |a| < m.

title: Transition Dynamics in General Two-Component Reaction-Diffusion Systems
summary: This work provides a comprehensive characterization of the first dynamic transition of a general two-component reaction-diffusion system on a bounded interval in one spatial dimension. By rigorously addressing the difficulties arising from the non-linear interactions between the two components, this study significantly extends the scope of previous studies on dynamic transitions of reaction-diffusion systems, which focused on single-equation cases. The analysis is conducted by employing center manifold reduction within the standard classification of dynamic transition theory. A key contribution of this study is that the nonlinear terms are treated to involve arbitrary powers of the unknowns $u$ and $v$. Furthermore, the theoretical framework is complemented by the analysis of a representative and simplified system. As a result of this generalization, the dynamics of a broad class of fundamental reaction-diffusion systems can be systematically classified.

AI.tldr: This paper characterizes the first dynamic transition of a general two-component reaction-diffusion system on a bounded 1D interval, extending prior single-equation results by handling nonlinear interactions between both components via center manifold reduction.
AI.motivation: Previous studies on dynamic transitions of reaction-diffusion systems focused only on single-equation cases. Extending this to two-component systems is difficult due to non-linear interactions between the two components, which this work aims to rigorously address.
AI.method: Center manifold reduction within the standard classification of dynamic transition theory is used. The nonlinear terms are treated to involve arbitrary powers of the unknowns u and v, and the framework is complemented by analysis of a representative simplified system.
AI.result: A comprehensive characterization of the first dynamic transition is obtained for a general two-component reaction-diffusion system on a bounded interval in one spatial dimension.
AI.conclusion: The generalization allows systematic classification of the dynamics of a broad class of fundamental reaction-diffusion systems, significantly extending previous single-equation studies.

title: Validation of Symmetry Induced Bifurcation Points in Nonlinear Diffusion Problems
summary: Nonlinear parabolic partial differential equations frequently occur in the modeling of applied phenomena. They often exhibit complicated dynamics which is organized by their associated equilibrium solutions. As a function of the involved model parameters, the equilibria can be detected using a bifurcation analysis, which in turn is centered around a deeper understanding of bifurcation points. In many applied systems establishing these organizing centers rigorously is difficult to achieve using traditional mathematical techniques. In this paper, we propose a theoretical framework for computer-assisted proofs of symmetry-induced transcritical and pitchfork bifurcations in nonlinear problems. This s accomplished by reformulating the existence question via a zero finding problem for an associated extended nonlinear system. The approach is general and allows for a wide variety of underlying symmetries. We demonstrate how these results can be applied in the setting of parabolic systems and higher-order equations, on both one- and two-dimensional domains.

AI.tldr: A computer-assisted proof framework is proposed to rigorously establish symmetry-induced transcritical and pitchfork bifurcations in nonlinear parabolic PDEs, via reformulating existence as a zero-finding problem for an extended nonlinear system.
AI.motivation: Nonlinear parabolic PDEs model applied phenomena and exhibit complex dynamics organized by equilibrium solutions. Rigorously establishing bifurcation points (the organizing centers) is difficult with traditional mathematical techniques.
AI.method: Reformulate the existence question as a zero-finding problem for an associated extended nonlinear system, yielding a general theoretical framework for computer-assisted proofs of symmetry-induced transcritical and pitchfork bifurcations, allowing a wide variety of underlying symmetries.
AI.result: The approach is general and is demonstrated in the setting of parabolic systems and higher-order equations, on both one- and two-dimensional domains.
AI.conclusion: A general, symmetry-flexible computer-assisted proof framework enables rigorous detection of transcritical and pitchfork bifurcations in nonlinear parabolic problems and higher-order equations.

title: The planarity estimate in dimensions five and six
summary: Naff's planarity estimate is a crucial tool for analysing singularities of quadratically pinched mean curvature flows in high codimension, showing that high-curvature regions become asymptotically codimension one. Naff established the estimate throughout the full Andrews--Baker pinching range in dimensions at least $7$, while in dimensions $5$ and $6$ a stronger pinching assumption was required. We close this remaining gap, proving the planarity estimate in dimensions $5$ and $6$ throughout the full Andrews--Baker range. The key new ingredient is a sharp Kato-type inequality relating the twisting of the principal normal to the gradient of the second fundamental form.

AI.tldr: This paper proves Naff's planarity estimate for quadratically pinched mean curvature flows in dimensions 5 and 6 across the full Andrews--Baker pinching range, closing a remaining gap via a sharp Kato-type inequality.
AI.motivation: Naff's planarity estimate is a key tool for analyzing singularities of quadratically pinched mean curvature flows in high codimension, showing high-curvature regions become asymptotically codimension one. Naff proved it over the full Andrews--Baker pinching range in dimensions ≥7, but dimensions 5 and 6 required a stronger pinching assumption, leaving a gap.
AI.method: The authors close this gap by introducing a sharp Kato-type inequality that relates the twisting of the principal normal to the gradient of the second fundamental form.
AI.result: The planarity estimate is established in dimensions 5 and 6 throughout the full Andrews--Baker range.
AI.conclusion: The remaining gap in Naff's planarity estimate for dimensions 5 and 6 is closed, extending the estimate to the full Andrews--Baker range in all dimensions.

title: Natural reparameterization and continuity of the solution map for polynomials
summary: The optimal Sobolev regularity of the roots of a smooth curve of monic complex polynomials is $W^{1,q}$, for $q \in [1,\frac{d}{d-1})$, where $d$ is the degree. This result is stable in the sense that the solution map from $C^d$ coefficients to $W^{1,q}$ roots is continuous. We prove that, after a natural Lipschitz reparameterization, the roots are Lipschitz and the map from $C^d$ coefficients to reparameterization and reparameterized roots is continuous with respect to the $W^{1,q}$ topology on the target spaces, for all $q \in [1,\infty)$. The result is based on a convergence and reparameterization theorem for Almgren's $Q$-valued Sobolev functions.

AI.tldr: Roots of a smooth curve of monic complex polynomials are Lipschitz after a natural Lipschitz reparameterization, and the reparameterization/root map is continuous in W^{1,q}, q∈[1,∞). This follows from a convergence and reparameterization theorem for Almgren's Q-valued Sobolev functions.
AI.motivation: Optimal Sobolev regularity of roots is W^{1,q} for q∈[1,d/(d-1)); this is stable via continuity of the solution map. The authors seek to improve regularity (to Lipschitz) via reparameterization and establish continuity of the reparameterized solution map in the W^{1,q} topology.
AI.method: Introduce a natural Lipschitz reparameterization and prove a convergence and reparameterization theorem for Almgren's Q-valued Sobolev functions, then apply it to the roots of a smooth curve of monic complex polynomials.
AI.result: After reparameterization, the roots are Lipschitz, and the map from C^d coefficients to reparameterization and reparameterized roots is continuous with respect to W^{1,q} on the target spaces, for all q∈[1,∞).
AI.conclusion: Reparameterization upgrades root regularity to Lipschitz and yields continuity in W^{1,q} for all q≥1, extending the known optimal Sobolev stability result.

title: Type I estimates for the Kahler-Ricci flow I
summary: We establish the Type I estimate for the scalar curvature of the Kahler-Ricci flow on compact Kahler manifolds, for arbitrary smooth initial metrics, whenever the flow develops finite time singularities. This estimate is a building block for the analytic minimal model program with Ricci flow.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes a Type I scalar curvature estimate for the Kähler-Ricci flow on compact Kähler manifolds with arbitrary smooth initial metrics when finite-time singularities form, serving as a building block for the analytic minimal model program.
AI.motivation: The analytic minimal model program with Ricci flow requires control on the blow-up behavior of curvature near finite-time singularities. A Type I scalar curvature estimate provides this crucial control and serves as a necessary building block for the program.
AI.method: The authors do not specify their methods in the abstract; the work is an analytic PDE study of the Kähler-Ricci flow, proving a Type I estimate for the scalar curvature on compact Kähler manifolds for arbitrary smooth initial metrics.
AI.result: A Type I estimate for the scalar curvature of the Kähler-Ricci flow is established whenever the flow develops finite-time singularities, holding for arbitrary smooth initial metrics on compact Kähler manifolds.
AI.conclusion: The Type I scalar curvature estimate provides a foundational component for the analytic minimal model program with Ricci flow.

title: The exact number of nonconstant positive solutions to the planar isotropic $L_p$ dual Minkowski problem
summary: We determine the exact number, up to rotations, of nonconstant positive $C^2$ solutions to the planar isotropic $L_p$ dual Minkowski problem for every $(p, q) \in \mathbb{R}^2$. We obtain a new parametrization of the associated period integral, characterize the regions where the period is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing, and prove that in the remaining nonmonotone region it has a unique nondegenerate maximum. As a consequence, we have a complete classification.

AI.tldr: The paper gives an exact count, up to rotations, of nonconstant positive C^2 solutions to the planar isotropic L_p dual Minkowski problem for all (p,q) in R^2, via a complete classification.
AI.motivation: The planar isotropic L_p dual Minkowski problem involves counting solutions, but a full classification over the entire (p,q) parameter plane was previously incomplete; the monotonicity behavior of the associated period integral needed clarification.
AI.method: Introduces a new parametrization of the associated period integral, characterizes regions where the period is strictly increasing or strictly decreasing, and proves the remaining nonmonotone region has a unique nondegenerate maximum.
AI.result: Characterizes the monotone regions (strict increase/decrease) of the period integral and shows the nonmonotone region has a unique nondegenerate maximum.
AI.conclusion: This yields a complete classification of the exact number of nonconstant positive C^2 solutions (up to rotations) for every (p,q) in R^2.

title: On critical dimensions for compactness in the boundary Yamabe problem, I
summary: We construct smooth, non-locally-conformally-flat metrics on the closed ball for which the boundary Yamabe equation admits $L^\infty$-unbounded sequences of positive solutions. The background metric and the prescribed scalar and boundary mean curvatures are fixed along each sequence. For zero scalar curvature and positive boundary mean curvature, such examples exist with umbilic boundary in every dimension $N\ge22$ and with nonumbilic boundary in every $N\ge15$. For positive scalar curvature and minimal boundary, the corresponding ranges are $N\ge21$ and $N\ge15$. For every $N\ge9$, examples with either umbilic or nonumbilic boundary also exist when the scalar curvature is $N(N-1)$ and the prescribed boundary mean curvature is below a negative threshold depending on $N$. The construction uses polynomial metric perturbations and corrected bubbles on the half-space, followed by conformal compactification to the ball. We evaluate or estimate the correction solving the linearized Neumann or Robin boundary problem and its contribution to the quadratic term of the reduced energy. We prove that this quadratic term has negative, nondegenerate local extrema with respect to tangential translations and scale in every stated dimension.

title: On the topology of the space of vacuum initial data sets
summary: We show that the space of vacuum initial data sets on a closed manifold often has many non-trivial homotopy groups. The starting point is a result of the second named author, which constructs non-trivial elements in the homotopy groups of the space of initial data sets satisfying the strict dominant energy condition, together with a later result in joint work with Bernd Ammann showing that these elements often persist when the strictness assumption is dropped. In this work, we use a parametrized version of the conformal method to show that these elements may also be represented by maps into the space of vacuum initial data sets. This requires two results that may be of independent interest: metrics admitting conformal Killing vectors can be removed from the space of metrics without changing its weak homotopy type, and over the remaining metrics the York decomposition can be carried out in families, the TT-tensors forming a trivial Hilbert bundle. To our knowledge, this is the first result on the global topology of this space.

title: Minimizing capture time with many small traps in heterogeneous media
summary: We study the problem of optimally placing a large number of small absorbing traps to minimize the mean first-passage time (MFPT) of particles diffusing in a heterogeneous medium with space-dependent diffusivity $D(x)$ and prescribed initial particle distribution $ω(x)$. In two and three dimensions we identify two distinct regimes, depending on how strongly the trap ensemble depletes the particles. In the weak trapping regime (fewer traps) the optimal trap density $ρ$ is the arithmetic average $ρ= \frac12(μ+ω)$ of the normalized inverse diffusivity $μ\propto 1/D$ and the initial particle distribution $ω$. In the strong trapping regime (more traps), it is proportional to their geometric average, $ρ\propto \sqrt{μω}$. We revisit the classical Green's function approach and show that it applies to weak trapping only; in 2D this requires the trap size to be exponentially small in the number of traps, so that most applications of interest fall in the strong trapping regime instead. We therefore develop a homogenization approach that captures both regimes. A special choice of initial particle distribution is $ω\propto 1/D$, which corresponds to the equilibrium particle distribution in the absence of traps according to the Itô interpretation. In this case we show that the optimal trap distribution is the stationary particle distribution itself, regardless of the trapping strength, and this makes the MFPT constant throughout the domain; the same trap distribution also minimizes the worst-case capture time. Finally, in one dimension we find instead $ρ\propto\left(μω\right) ^{1/3}$, and a similar analysis covers space-dependent drift and thin domains of variable cross-section. Direct numerical optimization confirms the analytical results.

The classical Green's function approach has limited validity.

title: Half-space KPZ equation from a class of nonlinear SPDEs
summary: We derive the half-space KPZ equation as a continuum limit from a general class of Ginzburg-Landau SPDEs under weak nonlinearity scaling. To our knowledge, this is the first half-space universality result for the KPZ equation beyond integrable models (and their perturbations).
